# Independent tombstone source foundation

The initial corpus is **15 pure safe/filename cases, 17 protocol cases and seven
main-loop transport cases**. All expected responses are independently executed
unchanged original source, not the Rust tombstoned/crash-reporting candidate.
Raw request/response JSON is stored as a string to retain the real decoder boundary
and lone-surrogate codepoints. There is no numeric or error-class normalization.

`provenance.json` seals nine retained policy/loader/worker inputs, original Python
version, the verified existing Params binding and its18 source inputs, and each
capture hash. Confirmation invokes the full unchanged original helper as a real
subprocess, including Worker construction, and uses actual stdin/stdout byte pipes.
No native candidate, AST constructor replacement or substituted text stream supplies
expected answers. Private capture script/raw bytes/receipts are retained under
`2026-10-19-version-load-source-closure/full-worker-pure-confirmation-2/`.

The earlier constructor seam omitted `MAX_TOMBSTONE_FN_LEN` and falsely produced
`AttributeError` for seven filename cases. Those invalid answers were replaced only
from full original Worker observations. Boolean filename paths still raise
`AttributeError`. Actual piped CR-only input produces one `JSONDecodeError` response;
the old substituted text stream incorrectly treated CR as a line separator. All17
protocol controls and the other six transport controls were confirmed unchanged.
The invalid prior captures remain archived privately; none is a native oracle.

The captured type boundaries include list/string iteration, invalid commit JSON,
falsey and list commits, a nonempty map's Python3.12 `KeyError` slice behavior,
non-string paths, numeric dates and lone-surrogate values. In particular, original
tombstoned `main` catches unknown-operation `AssertionError` and continues; the
Version source transport has a different contract and must not be reused blindly.

This is a test-first foundation toward the existing full **242-call** independent
Sentry/tombstone Worker/controller. Configure/reporting gates, Params writes,
SDK-call ordering, files/scans/cycles/retrace, real logging, actual runtime shutdown
and managed-entry/HTTP SDK consumers remain pending. No original is deleted.

Proposed API after parent observes missing-module RED:

```rust
pub fn sources(repository: &Path) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, String>>;
pub struct Session { /* independent source state */ }
impl Session {
    pub fn new(cwd: &Path, environment: &BTreeMap<OsString, OsString>) -> Result<Self>;
    pub fn request(&mut self, raw_json: &[u8]) -> Result<JsonValue>;
}
pub fn source(cwd: &Path, environment: &BTreeMap<OsString, OsString>,
              input: &mut dyn BufRead, output: &mut dyn Write) -> Result<()>;
```

`request` returns the original full worker record `{result, calls, logs}`. Ordinary
protocol/policy exceptions are recorded inside `result.error`, not a native outer
error. Future process cancellation/deadline is a controller abort instead. Source
implementation may reuse mechanical lossless JSON and independent Version Session,
but must not call candidate tombstoned/Reporter/managed-entry to calculate answers.

The parent registered the required `tombstone-tools-native` test and observed the
genuine E0432 missing-module RED before implementation. The source foundation now
implements these captured pure/protocol cases; its first compilation and GREEN
remain pending. It does not read expected fixtures or call candidate runtime
code. Generic independent JSON/representation helpers preserve Python values, and
`unicode-general-category = "=0.6.0"` supplies the same Unicode15.0 classification
as Python3.12. This existing locked dependency needs parent-owned registration.

Known stateful operations (configure/init/SDK/files/daemon cycles) currently return
an explicit OUTER `UnsupportedSourceOperation`, rather than counterfeit original
error rows or candidate results. Unknown protocol operations retain the captured
ordinary `AssertionError` result. The full242 Worker remains the next objective;
these foundation tests are not full source or tool retirement.

## Stateful test-first extension

Three separately sealed fixtures add **72 original calls**: all50 original Sentry
reporting gates, nine partial-configure/Params identity controls, and13 tag controls.
`stateful-provenance.json` binds the unchanged full original Worker and policies,
the already-built original Params binding and its source provenance, raw capture
receipts and the three fixture hashes. No native runtime supplies expected answers.

The filesystem replay was independently executed again through the full unchanged
original Worker for all72 calls before writing the permanent native tests. It
preserves actual file writes, unlinks, directory/file permission errors, invalid
UTF8 DongleId, registered/PC/origin gates, both project integration choices, typed
metadata, real CarrotException bytes and SDK observation order. Partial configure
errors retain exactly the original preceding assignments; SDK failure/reset and
recovery remain observable across requests. Tags include lossless lone-surrogate
values and malformed JSON. SDK arrays and logs retain their original order;
`value_json` is decoded only as the original comparator does, and only dynamic
`created` timestamps are excluded from value equality (their fields/types remain).

This group does **not** cover the remaining192 original file/scanner/loop/parser/
retrace cases, real runtime/managed-entry ownership, or retirement. New permanent
stateful tests are source-ready; their native RED/GREEN and strict Clippy are
pending a parent compiler lease. No original tools have been removed.

## Original file/scanner/retrace extension

Three additional Linux tests preserve **44 original calls**: files33, scan6 and
subprocess5. `files-provenance.json` seals the unchanged original full Worker
capture, all source inputs, the three expected fixtures and the exact original
`apport-retrace` helper bytes (tracked executable, symlinked into private fixtures).
The fixture actions were replayed independently through the full unchanged original
Worker for all44 calls, including the real30second timeout. No candidate executed.

The reports retain actual file hashes/sizes/explicit modes, UTF8 read-ahead failures,
CR/newline parsing, Unicode/signed/underscored signal text, command decode-before-exit
errors, permission/copy/same-file behavior, nested destination semantics, and both
100,000,001-byte rejection and100,000,000-byte accepted copy/delete boundary. Large
inputs are real sparse files, not canned report replies. Hashing uses a bounded
buffer; the test checks the25GiB reserve plus256MiB growth before creating them.

Scanner expected names and ctime use actual live pre-call directory enumeration and
followed-target stat metadata according to the retained original predicate/order:
consume the first1000 entries before filtering, exact regular mode0o100640, or the
`tombstone` prefix. Historical raw names/epochs remain immutable in the fixture.
The new fixture's actual enumeration and ctimes are bound independently, rather than
assuming historical filesystem order/epoch values or sorting before truncation.
Default file/directory modes bind to fresh same-process probes, preserving the
caller's real umask without changing it; explicit chmod/copied modes stay exact.

Actual timeout requests remain100ms,100ms and30,000ms. The native regression also
requires no surviving timeout helper; failure cleanup uses a live pidfd checked
against its private fixture token. It does not reproduce the original leaked-helper
cleanup defect. This is test-first source preparation; native RED/GREEN and strict
Clippy for the extension are pending. The remaining14 loop and134 text calls are
not claimed covered by this44-call group. No original tools have been retired.

## Complete original242 test-source roster

Three final Linux tests add **148 original calls**: text134, reporting-loop7 and
disabled-loop7. The roster is now gates50 +files33 +scan6 +reporting-loop7
+disabled-loop7 +text134 +subprocess5 = **242**. The foundation39 protocol/pure/
transport controls and22 extra configure/tag controls remain additional tests;
they are not counted toward those242 calls.

`remaining-provenance.json` seals the original full-source receipt, policies,
expected fixtures and the fresh replay proving all148 actions against the full
unchanged original Worker. The original Worker ran its actual thread/main function,
asserted the monkeypatched sleep argument is5, and synchronized each start/cycle
response through its actual queues. No candidate or test-produced policy answer
was used. The134 text calls retain the entire original seeded Unicode input list
and all typed/falsey/sequence commit cases, without regenerating random inputs.

Loop cases preserve initial hidden/ordinary file cleanup, initialization/SDK calls,
per-cycle observed file sets, no-repeat empty cycles, unknown and malformed crashes,
subsequent new files and reporting-disabled deletion. Raw Unix filenames remain
exact bytes in filesystem actions; expected file snapshots and source replies use
lossless JSON strings, so surrogateescape names are never narrowed through serde
String/Value. Snapshots check actual hashes, sizes and permission semantics.

Only cycle logs are sorted using the original comparator's created-stripped,
key-sorted JSON rule. SDK call order and noncycle log order remain exact. Each
source Session is dropped before its temporary filesystem owner is released.
No real five-second wait is invented: the original source helper intentionally
pauses at the five-second sleep boundary via queues, which the replay verifies.

These tests and source-only fixtures are ready. Native implementation, RED/GREEN,
strict Clippy and full tool/controller/SDK/managed-entry retirement remain pending.
The completed242 roster is not a native pass or permission to remove originals.
